sources.title: Aarhus University: Viking Age royal politics
sources.note: Sections Godfred’s wars, travellers in the 890s, and Sven/Cnut. Contemporary geographical scope uncertain, multiple simultaneous kings. No adoption of erroneous 858/859 Gorm mound date or speculative tax-name etymology elsewhere on page.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: magnates’ residences and royal seats
sources.note: Lejre Viking settlement and 48 by 11 metre hall; palisade and workshops. Avoid superlative largest hall because subsequent discoveries exceed this older example.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Viking blót sacrifices
sources.note: Tissø great hall animal bones and drinking-glass fragments, heat-affected stone pile. Feast interpretation supported; exact solstice rituals speculative and omitted.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Viking ring fortresses
sources.note: Geometrical layouts, four gates, timber ring dating. Trelleborg date 980 to 981 used; not imposed on all forts, since Fyrkat chronology differs in newer Aarhus account.

sources.title: Barfod, Feveile and Sindbæk: Splinters to splendours, 2022
sources.note: Peer-reviewed primary research abstract; 90 analyzed glass pieces from two eighth-century workshops. White beads made from remelted gold-leaf tesserae and air bubbles; university press account also checked, same-work budget.

sources.title: Lisbeth Imer and Søren Sindbæk: Nye fund af runer i Ribe, 2021
sources.note: Printed pp 11 to 13, fig 3. Full paper read via author-publication mirror https://www.arild-hauge.com/PDF/Nye_fund_af_runer_i_Ribe.pdf; downloaded and visually checked figure 3 in cache. DK SJy81 / X536, first half ninth century. Reindeer antler, iron rivets, 17 cm surviving length, inscription kąbaʀ = comb. Typed runes are standardized rendering, not facsimile.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Viking homes
sources.note: The farm, longhouse and smoky houses sections. General Danish Viking-period reconstruction; no exact universal village size, disease rate or window prohibition copied.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: children in the Viking period
sources.note: Toys and tasks sections. General Viking-period finds and reconstruction. No Icelandic legal adulthood rules or unsupported mortality totals transferred to Danish children.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Viking health
sources.note: Opening discussion of skeletal joint/tooth damage and limits of plant-remedy evidence. No sweeping life-expectancy statistic reproduced.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: the Jelling Stone
sources.note: Large stone around 965, Harald’s parents and Christian claim; Christianity present before royal monument. Does not treat royal boast as instantaneous national conversion.
